newsitem.title: USA: US FDA drug approvals up sharply in 1996.
newsitem.headline: US FDA drug approvals up sharply in 1996.

text.p: The Food and Drug Administration said Tuesday it approved 139 new drugs and biological products in 1996, a 63-percent increase from 1995.
The 1996 approvals were the largest amount since approval procedures became stricter in 1962, a spokeswoman said.
The FDA attributed the jump to the Prescription Drug User Fee Act, which allows the U.S. drug regulatory agency to charge manufacturers fees to shorten the drug review and approval time.
The shortening of approval time was "achieved without sacrificing the agency's high review standards," the FDA said in a statement.
The agency said that 131 new drugs were approved within the median time of 15.4 months, up 60 percent from the 82 approved within the same period in 1995.
Fifty-three of the drugs were new molecular entities, products containing an active substance that had never before been approved for marketing in any form in the United States.
Nine of the drugs with new molecular entities, including three AIDS therapies and two cancer drugs, were approved in six months or less.

Crixivan, a protease inhibitor for the treatment of AIDS created by Merck & Co Inc, was approved in 1.4 months. Abbott Laboratories Inc's Norvir and Boehringer Ingelheim 's Viramune, also AIDS treatments, were both approved in less than four months.
The FDA said it also approved several cancer drugs, including drugs for ovarian cancer, breast cancer, cancer of the pancreas and prostate cancer.
Medications were also approved for the treatment of asthma, Alzheimer's disease and multiple sclerosis, FDA said.
In the area of biologics, first-time approvals included a vaccine and seven therapeutic products. Biologic products were approved in 1996 15 percent faster than in 1995, FDA said.

Biologic approvals include five new test kits for HIV, the virust that causes AIDS, and two home collection kits, which allow people to collect their own blood samples, send it to a lab and receive the results by telephone.
